Alice — thanks for the redline. Looping in Legal (Olga) and Contracts (Laura) to run the detailed review. Quick high-level from my side after a skim: 

1) Roles: the controller/processor split is mostly fine but we should avoid blanket controller language that imposes additional liabilities on Redwood beyond the order form. Olga — can you suggest precise alternative wording for §2 that preserves customer's controls but keeps our liability carveouts?

2) SCC references: the redline points to the 2021 Clauses plus an extra audit right. We can accept SCC incorporation but need to limit audit scope and incorporate the standard 30-day remediation window.

3) Subprocessors: we will provide our current subprocessor roster, but GlobalHealth's proposed approval flow is too manual. Can we propose a 10-business-day notice + objection flow (auto-approval at day 11) to avoid gating onboarding?

4) Transfer-impact addendum: procurement asks for it to be bundled into the order form as an annex. That should be OK but may require a small SOW amendment (pricing impact TBD).

Next steps I propose: 
- Olga to produce line-by-line comments and suggested language by Tue EOD (2026-08-31).
- Laura to capture any order-form sequencing or signature-path implications for Dedicated vs Hosted.
- I'll own scheduling a 30-min sync with GlobalHealth for Wed morning (proposed times below).

Thanks team — I put some initial notes in the attached.

Regards,

Team / Alice — attaching a short legal note and suggested clause language (DPA_clause_suggestions.docx). High level comments inline below and in the attachment.

On Sun, Aug 30, 2026 at 09:12 Alice Turner <alice.turner@globalhealth.example.com> wrote:
> (GlobalHealth redline attached)

Our proposed updates: 

- §2 (Roles): Replace "Redwood is a processor" language with: 
  "Redwood shall process Personal Data only on behalf of Customer and in accordance with the Order Form and documented instructions. Redwood's processing obligations shall be limited to the provision of the Services and shall not extend to activities outside that scope. Redwood's aggregate liability under this DPA shall be subject to the liability cap set forth in the MSA."

- SCCs: We will accept incorporation of the EU SCCs (2021) provided we insert a paragraph limiting on-site audits to a Party's right to request evidence and to a remote review as first step. Proposed text added at Clause 7.

- Subprocessor approvals: We cannot commit to per-subprocessor pre-approval for all categories. Proposed operational flow: Redwood publishes subprocessors on a public roster; Customer has 10 business days to object in writing; failure to object = deemed consent. For high-risk subprocessors (as defined in Annex X), pre-notice and additional controls will apply.

- Transfer-impact addendum: Legal prefers adding the transfer-impact annex as an appendix to the Order Form rather than changing the MSA. That reduces scope creep. Laura — confirm if procurement needs a separate DocuSign envelope for the annex.

Open questions for GlobalHealth: 
1) Can you confirm the list of jurisdictions where export controls are a concern (UK + Germany + Finland listed in your redline?)
2) Any subprocessors you expect to require pre-approval? If so, please list them.

I'll circulate a tracked-changes DPA back to Alice by EOD today for a final pass.

--
